Found two concrete issues worth fixing, both directly evidenced in the code:

1. **A real bug**: `stats.Mean` in `stats/stats.go` starts its summing loop at index 1, silently skipping the first element of every input. This means `Mean([2,4,6])` returns `3.33...` instead of `4` — and the existing test case for exactly that input (`TestMean`/"several") should already be failing.
2. **A promised-but-missing feature**: README's Status section and a `// TODO` comment in `stats.go` both explicitly say Median is planned but not implemented.

I'm proposing 3 beads: fix the Mean bug (highest priority — it's silently producing wrong output), implement Median in the stats package with tests, then wire Median into the CLI output and update the README status (depends on the Median implementation). These are independently scoped and match what the repo itself is asking for — no invented work.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).
beads.acceptance: stats.Median([]float64{}) returns ErrEmpty. stats.Median([]float64{3}) returns 3. stats.Median([]float64{1,3,2}) returns 2 (unsorted odd-length input is sorted internally). stats.Median([]float64{1,2,3,4}) returns 2.5 (even-length: average of the two middle sorted values). A slice passed to Median is not mutated or reordered by the call (verified by a test that checks the original slice's order/contents after calling Median). New unit tests covering empty, single-element, unsorted odd-length, and even-length cases are added to stats/stats_test.go. `go test ./...` passes.

I didn't find other credible bugs or missing features beyond what's already tracked — this is intentionally a minimal fixture, so I kept the plan to these two evidenced items rather than padding it out.

bead.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
bead.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
bead.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

bead.title: Add test coverage for the fixture CLI's argument parsing and error paths
bead.description: Only stats/ has a test suite (stats/stats_test.go); main.go, which parses CLI args and prints sum/mean/max with specific exit codes on bad input or a missing argument list, currently has zero test coverage. That means the documented CLI contract (usage message + exit code 2 for no args, "<arg> is not a number" + exit code 2 for a bad number, formatted success output) can regress silently. Add a test file (e.g. main_test.go), either by invoking the built binary via os/exec or by extracting the parsing/formatting logic into a testable helper, covering the golden path and both documented error paths.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).
beads.acceptance: stats.Median([]float64{}) returns ErrEmpty. stats.Median([]float64{3}) returns 3. stats.Median([]float64{1,3,2}) returns 2 (unsorted odd-length input is sorted internally). stats.Median([]float64{1,2,3,4}) returns 2.5 (even-length: average of the two middle sorted values). A slice passed to Median is not mutated or reordered by the call (verified by a test that checks the original slice's order/contents after calling Median). New unit tests covering empty, single-element, unsorted odd-length, and even-length cases are added to stats/stats_test.go. `go test ./...` passes.

plan.brief: Reading stats/stats.go turned up a real, currently-failing bug: Mean's summation loop starts at index 1 instead of 0 (stats/stats.go:24), so it silently ignores the first element of any multi-value input. The existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) computes the true mean, so this bug should be making `go test ./...` fail right now, not just a latent risk. This is distinct from the four open beads (Max bug, Median implementation/printing, CLI arg parsing tests), so it's proposed as a single, well-scoped fix. No other unaddressed, evidence-backed work was found in this small repo, so only one bead is proposed rather than padding the plan.

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
beads.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).
beads.acceptance: stats.Median([]float64{}) returns ErrEmpty. stats.Median([]float64{3}) returns 3. stats.Median([]float64{1,3,2}) returns 2 (unsorted odd-length input is sorted internally). stats.Median([]float64{1,2,3,4}) returns 2.5 (even-length: average of the two middle sorted values). beads.title: Add test coverage for the fixture CLI's argument parsing and error paths
beads.description: Only stats/ has a test suite (stats/stats_test.go); main.go, which parses CLI args and prints sum/mean/max with specific exit codes on bad input or a missing argument list, currently has zero test coverage. beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
beads.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).
beads.acceptance: stats.Median([]float64{}) returns ErrEmpty. stats.Median([]float64{3}) returns 3. stats.Median([]float64{1,3,2}) returns 2 (unsorted odd-length input is sorted internally). stats.Median([]float64{1,2,3,4}) returns 2.5 (even-length: average of the two middle sorted values). A slice passed to Median is not mutated or reordered by the call (verified by a test that checks the original slice's order/contents after calling Median). New unit tests covering empty, single-element, unsorted odd-length, and even-length cases are added to stats/stats_test.go. `go test ./...` passes.

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
beads.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

bead.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 for all-negative inputs
bead.description: stats.Max (stats/stats.go:31-42) seeds its `largest` accumulator with the float64 zero value and only updates it when a value is strictly greater. For a slice where every value is negative, no element ever exceeds 0, so the function returns 0 instead of the true maximum. The existing test case TestMax/all_negative (stats/stats_test.go, values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) already encodes the correct expected behavior and currently fails against this implementation. Fix Max to seed the accumulator with the first element of the slice (e.g. `largest := values[0]` and iterate from index 1) so it works correctly for any sign of input, keeping the existing ErrEmpty behavior for empty slices.

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max (stats/stats.go:31-42) seeds its `largest` accumulator with the float64 zero value and only updates it when a value is strictly greater. For a slice where every value is negative, no element ever exceeds 0, so the function returns 0 instead of the true maximum. The existing test case TestMax/all_negative (stats/stats_test.go, values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) already encodes the correct expected behavior and currently fails against this implementation. Fix Max to seed the accumulator with the first element of the slice (e.g. `largest := values[0]` and iterate from index 1) so it works correctly for any sign of input, keeping the existing ErrEmpty behavior for empty slices.
beads.acceptance: go test ./... passes, including the existing TestMax/all_negative subtest which must return -1 for Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) instead of 0. Max continues to return ErrEmpty for an empty input slice, and existing TestMax/single and TestMax/positive subtests still pass unchanged.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
beads.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).
beads.acceptance: stats.Median([]float64{}) returns ErrEmpty. stats.Median([]float64{3}) returns 3. stats.Median([]float64{1,3,2}) returns 2 (unsorted odd-length input is sorted internally). stats.Median([]float64{1,2,3,4}) returns 2.5 (even-length: average of the two middle sorted values). A slice passed to Median is not mutated or reordered by the call (verified by a test that checks the original slice's order/contents after calling Median). New unit tests covering empty, single-element, unsorted odd-length, and even-length cases are added to stats/stats_test.go. `go test ./...` passes.

beads.title: Add test coverage for the fixture CLI's argument parsing and error paths
beads.description: Only stats/ has a test suite (stats/stats_test.go); main.go, which parses CLI args and prints sum/mean/max with specific exit codes on bad input or a missing argument list, currently has zero test coverage. That means the documented CLI contract (usage message + exit code 2 for no args, "<arg> is not a number" + exit code 2 for a bad number, formatted success output) can regress silently. Add a test file (e.g. main_test.go), either by invoking the built binary via os/exec or by extracting the parsing/formatting logic into a testable helper, covering the golden path and both documented error paths.
beads.acceptance: A new test file exercises: (a) running with no arguments exits with status 2 and prints the "usage: fixture NUMBER [NUMBER...]" message to stderr; (b) running with a non-numeric argument exits with status 2 and prints a "fixture: ... is not a number" message to stderr naming the bad argument; (c) running with valid numeric arguments exits 0 and prints output to stdout containing correctly computed sum, mean, and max values. `make test` / `go test ./...` passes including the new tests. No change to main.go's existing documented CLI behaviour is required by this bead.

beads.description: Only stats/ has a test suite (stats/stats_test.go); main.go, which parses CLI args and prints sum/mean/max with specific exit codes on bad input or a missing argument list, currently has zero test coverage. That means the documented CLI contract (usage message + exit code 2 for no args, "<arg> is not a number" + exit code 2 for a bad number, formatted success output) can regress silently. Add a test file (e.g. main_test.go), either by invoking the built binary via os/exec or by extracting the parsing/formatting logic into a testable helper, covering the golden path and both documented error paths.
beads.acceptance: A new test file exercises: (a) running with no arguments exits with status 2 and prints the "usage: fixture NUMBER [NUMBER...]" message to stderr; (b) running with a non-numeric argument exits with status 2 and prints a "fixture: ... is not a number" message to stderr naming the bad argument; (c) running with valid numeric arguments exits 0 and prints output to stdout containing correctly computed sum, mean, and max values. `make test` / `go test ./...` passes including the new tests. No change to main.go's existing documented CLI behaviour is required by this bead.

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max (stats/stats.go:31-42) seeds its `largest` accumulator with the float64 zero value and only updates it when a value is strictly greater. For a slice where every value is negative, no element ever exceeds 0, so the function returns 0 instead of the true maximum. The existing test case TestMax/all_negative (stats/stats_test.go, values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) already encodes the correct expected behavior and currently fails against this implementation. Fix Max to seed the accumulator with the first element of the slice (e.g. `largest := values[0]` and iterate from index 1) so it works correctly for any sign of input, keeping the existing ErrEmpty behavior for empty slices.
beads.acceptance: go test ./... passes, including the existing TestMax/all_negative subtest which must return -1 for Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) instead of 0. Max continues to return ErrEmpty for an empty input slice, and existing TestMax/single and TestMax/positive subtests still pass unchanged.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
beads.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max (stats/stats.go:31-42) seeds its `largest` accumulator with the float64 zero value and only updates it when a value is strictly greater. For a slice where every value is negative, no element ever exceeds 0, so the function returns 0 instead of the true maximum. The existing test case TestMax/all_negative (stats/stats_test.go, values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) already encodes the correct expected behavior and currently fails against this implementation. Fix Max to seed the accumulator with the first element of the slice (e.g. `largest := values[0]` and iterate from index 1) so it works correctly for any sign of input, keeping the existing ErrEmpty behavior for empty slices.
beads.acceptance: go test ./... passes, including the existing TestMax/all_negative subtest which must return -1 for Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) instead of 0. Max continues to return ErrEmpty for an empty input slice, and existing TestMax/single and TestMax/positive subtests still pass unchanged.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
beads.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).

A slice passed to Median is not mutated or reordered by the call (verified by a test that checks the original slice's order/contents after calling Median). line: Research done. Two real findings beyond the already-tracked Max bug:

1. **`stats.Mean` has an off-by-one bug** — its summation loop starts at `i := 1`, so `values[0]` is never added. Tracing it by hand: `Mean([]float64{7})` returns `0` (not `7`), and `Mean([]float64{2,4,6})` returns `3.333...` (not `4`). The existing `TestMean` subtests "single" and "several" in `stats/stats_test.go` encode the correct expected values, so this is a live correctness bug, not a hypothetical one.

2. **`Median` is promised but missing** — the README's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet," and `stats/stats.go` has a literal `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` marker. This is a real, self-declared gap.

I'm proposing the Mean fix (highest priority — it's a shipped correctness bug), then implementing Median, then a small dependent bead to wire Median into the CLI output and README, since main.go currently only prints sum/mean/max.

Update main.go to compute and print the median alongside the existing output, handling the ErrEmpty case the same way the existing Max error is handled today. Update the README usage example to mention that median is printed.

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first value due to off-by-one loop
beads.description: In stats/stats.go, Mean's summation loop starts at index 1 instead of 0 (`for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`), so values[0] is never added to the total. Hand-tracing confirms this is wrong: Mean([]float64{7}) currently returns 0 instead of 7, and Mean([]float64{2,4,6}) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing table-driven TestMean in stats/stats_test.go already encodes the correct expected values for its "single" and "several" subtests, so this bug causes those tests to fail. Fix the loop to include all elements (start at index 0, or use a range loop) so the sum is correct.
beads.acceptance: Mean's loop iterates over all elements starting at index 0 (e.g. `for i := 0; i < len(values); i++` or `for _, v := range values`). `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "single" ({7} -> 7) and "several" ({2,4,6} -> 4) subtests. Mean's signature and its empty-input behavior (returns 0 for empty input) are unchanged.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max (stats/stats.go:31-42) seeds its `largest` accumulator with the float64 zero value and only updates it when a value is strictly greater. For a slice where every value is negative, no element ever exceeds 0, so the function returns 0 instead of the true maximum. The existing test case TestMax/all_negative (stats/stats_test.go, values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) already encodes the correct expected behavior and currently fails against this implementation. Fix Max to seed the accumulator with the first element of the slice (e.g. `largest := values[0]` and iterate from index 1) so it works correctly for any sign of input, keeping the existing ErrEmpty behavior for empty slices.
beads.acceptance: go test ./... passes, including the existing TestMax/all_negative subtest which must return -1 for Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) instead of 0. Max continues to return ErrEmpty for an empty input slice, and existing TestMax/single and TestMax/positive subtests still pass unchanged.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
beads.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median as promised by the README
beads.description: The README's Status section states "Median is planned but not implemented yet," and stats/stats.go contains a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` marker with no corresponding function. Add a Median function to the stats package following the conventions already used by Sum/Mean/Max, including returning stats.ErrEmpty for empty input (consistent with Max), correctly handling both odd- and even-length inputs (average the two middle values for even-length), and without mutating the caller's input slice (sort a copy internally). Add table-driven tests in stats/stats_test.go covering odd-length, even-length, single-element, unsorted-input, and empty-input cases.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).
beads.acceptance: stats.Median([]float64{}) returns ErrEmpty. stats.Median([]float64{3}) returns 3. stats.Median([]float64{1,3,2}) returns 2 (unsorted odd-length input is sorted internally). stats.Median([]float64{1,2,3,4}) returns 2.5 (even-length: average of the two middle sorted values). A slice passed to Median is not mutated or reordered by the call (verified by a test that checks the original slice's order/contents after calling Median). New unit tests covering empty, single-element, unsorted odd-length, and even-length cases are added to stats/stats_test.go. `go test ./...` passes.

beads.title: Add test coverage for the fixture CLI's argument parsing and error paths
beads.description: Only stats/ has a test suite (stats/stats_test.go); main.go, which parses CLI args and prints sum/mean/max with specific exit codes on bad input or a missing argument list, currently has zero test coverage. beads.acceptance: A new test file exercises: (a) running with no arguments exits with status 2 and prints the "usage: fixture NUMBER [NUMBER...]" message to stderr; (b) running with a non-numeric argument exits with status 2 and prints a "fixture: ... is not a number" message to stderr naming the bad argument; (c) running with valid numeric arguments exits 0 and prints output to stdout containing correctly computed sum, mean, and max values. `make test` / `go test ./...` passes including the new tests. No change to main.go's existing documented CLI behaviour is required by this bead.

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first element of its input
beads.description: stats.Mean (stats/stats.go:19-28) loops `for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`, which starts at index 1 and never adds values[0] into the running total. As a result, Mean returns the wrong value for any input with more than one element (e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4). The existing TestMean test in stats/stats_test.go already asserts the correct mean for a multi-value case ({2,4,6} -> want 4), so this bug should currently be causing `go test ./...` to fail. Since Mean is used directly by the CLI (main.go) to print `mean=...` output, this also means the command-line tool is printing incorrect statistics today. Fix the loop to start at index 0 (or otherwise sum all elements) so Mean returns the correct arithmetic mean.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean sums every element of its input (including index 0). `go test ./...` passes, including the existing TestMean 'several' case ({2,4,6} -> want 4) with no changes needed to the test's expectations. Running `go run . 2 4 6` prints `mean=4` (not 3.33333...). No other exported behavior of the stats package changes.

beads.title: Fix off-by-one bug in stats.Mean that skips the first value
beads.description: stats.Mean's summing loop in stats/stats.go starts at index 1 instead of 0, so the first element of the input slice is never added to the total. This makes Mean() return an incorrect result for every non-empty input — e.g. Mean([2,4,6]) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing test case in stats_test.go (TestMean, subtest "several", values {2,4,6}, want 4) exercises exactly this input and should currently be failing because of this bug. Fix the loop in stats/stats.go so it includes index 0.
beads.acceptance: stats.Mean in stats/stats.go sums every element of the input slice, starting at index 0. `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "several" subtest ({2,4,6} -> 4). Mean(nil) still returns 0 (empty case unchanged).

beads.title: Fix stats.Mean skipping the first value due to off-by-one loop
beads.description: In stats/stats.go, Mean's summation loop starts at index 1 instead of 0 (`for i := 1; i < len(values); i++`), so values[0] is never added to the total. Hand-tracing confirms this is wrong: Mean([]float64{7}) currently returns 0 instead of 7, and Mean([]float64{2,4,6}) currently returns 3.333... instead of 4. The existing table-driven TestMean in stats/stats_test.go already encodes the correct expected values for its "single" and "several" subtests, so this bug causes those tests to fail. Fix the loop to include all elements (start at index 0, or use a range loop) so the sum is correct.
beads.acceptance: Mean's loop iterates over all elements starting at index 0 (e.g. `for i := 0; i < len(values); i++` or `for _, v := range values`). `go test ./...` passes, including TestMean's "single" ({7} -> 7) and "several" ({2,4,6} -> 4) subtests. Mean's signature and its empty-input behavior (returns 0 for empty input) are unchanged.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max (stats/stats.go:31-42) seeds its `largest` accumulator with the float64 zero value and only updates it when a value is strictly greater. For a slice where every value is negative, no element ever exceeds 0, so the function returns 0 instead of the true maximum. The existing test case TestMax/all_negative (stats/stats_test.go, values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) already encodes the correct expected behavior and currently fails against this implementation. Fix Max to seed the accumulator with the first element of the slice (e.g. `largest := values[0]` and iterate from index 1) so it works correctly for any sign of input, keeping the existing ErrEmpty behavior for empty slices.
beads.acceptance: go test ./... passes, including the existing TestMax/all_negative subtest which must return -1 for Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) instead of 0. Max continues to return ErrEmpty for an empty input slice, and existing TestMax/single and TestMax/positive subtests still pass unchanged.

beads.title: Fix stats.Max returning 0 instead of largest value for all-negative inputs
beads.description: stats.Max in stats/stats.go initializes `largest` to the zero value of float64 (0) and only updates it when a value is strictly greater than the current largest. When every input value is negative, no value ever exceeds 0, so Max silently returns 0 instead of the true maximum (the least-negative value). This already makes stats/stats_test.go's TestMax/all_negative case (values {-3, -1, -7}, want -1) fail, so `go test ./...` does not currently pass cleanly. Fix Max to seed `largest` from the first element of values and compare the rest against it, rather than seeding from the zero value.
beads.acceptance: stats.Max([]float64{-3, -1, -7}) returns (-1, nil). stats.Max([]float64{-3}) returns (-3, nil). All existing TestMax cases in stats/stats_test.go (single, positive, all negative) pass. stats.Max still returns (0, ErrEmpty) for an empty input slice. `go test ./...` passes with no failures.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median as promised by the README
beads.description: The README's Status section states "Median is planned but not implemented yet," and stats/stats.go contains a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` marker with no corresponding function. Add a Median function to the stats package following the conventions already used by Sum/Mean/Max, including returning stats.ErrEmpty for empty input (consistent with Max), correctly handling both odd- and even-length inputs (average the two middle values for even-length), and without mutating the caller's input slice (sort a copy internally). Add table-driven tests in stats/stats_test.go covering odd-length, even-length, single-element, unsorted-input, and empty-input cases.
beads.acceptance: stats.Median(values []float64) (float64, error) is implemented in stats/stats.go and returns stats.ErrEmpty for empty input, matching Max's error convention. Median of an odd-length slice returns the middle value once sorted; median of an even-length slice returns the average of the two middle values once sorted. Calling Median does not mutate the caller's original slice. New tests in stats/stats_test.go cover odd-length, even-length, single-element, unsorted-input, and empty-input cases, and go test ./... passes. The README's Status section is updated to state that Median is now implemented.

beads.title: Print median in fixture CLI output and update README status
beads.description: Once stats.Median exists, the fixture CLI (main.go) should print it alongside sum, mean, and max, matching the tool's existing output convention. README.md's Status section currently states Median is "planned but not implemented yet" and should be updated to reflect that it is now implemented alongside Sum, Mean, and Max.
beads.acceptance: Running `go run . 3 1 4 1 5` prints a single line including sum, mean, max, and median values in the style `sum=... mean=... max=... median=...`. README.md's Status section no longer says Median is planned/not implemented; it states Median is implemented along with Sum, Mean, and Max. `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` both succeed.

beads.title: Implement stats.Median
beads.description: README.md's Status section says "Median is planned but not implemented yet", and stats/stats.go has a `// TODO: implement Median; the README promises it.` comment. Add a Median function to stats/stats.go following the existing package conventions: same style as Sum/Mean/Max, returning (float64, error) and ErrEmpty for empty input (matching Max's signature). It must correctly handle both odd-length input (return the middle value of the sorted slice) and even-length input (return the average of the two middle values of the sorted slice), and must not mutate or reorder the caller's original slice (copy before sorting).
beads.acceptance: stats.Median([]float64{}) returns ErrEmpty. stats.Median([]float64{3}) returns 3. stats.Median([]float64{1,3,2}) returns 2 (unsorted odd-length input is sorted internally). stats.Median([]float64{1,2,3,4}) returns 2.5 (even-length: average of the two middle sorted values). A slice passed to Median is not mutated or reordered by the call (verified by a test that checks the original slice's order/contents after calling Median). New unit tests covering empty, single-element, unsorted odd-length, and even-length cases are added to stats/stats_test.go. `go test ./...` passes.

beads.title: Print median in the fixture CLI output
beads.description: main.go currently computes and prints sum, mean, and max but omits median, even though stats.Median (added by implement-median) makes this straightforward. Update main.go to compute and print the median alongside the existing output, handling the ErrEmpty case the same way the existing Max error is handled today. Update the README usage example to mention that median is printed.
beads.acceptance: main.go calls stats.Median and includes its result in the printed output line (e.g. `sum=... mean=... median=... max=...`), with ErrEmpty handled the same way the current Max error is handled. README's Usage section is updated to mention median in the example output. go build ./... and go test ./... succeed, and running `go run . 3 1 4 1 5` prints a median value in its output.

beads.title: Add test coverage for the fixture CLI's argument parsing and error paths
beads.description: Only stats/ has a test suite (stats/stats_test.go); main.go, which parses CLI args and prints sum/mean/max with specific exit codes on bad input or a missing argument list, currently has zero test coverage. That means the documented CLI contract (usage message + exit code 2 for no args, "<arg> is not a number" + exit code 2 for a bad number, formatted success output) can regress silently. Add a test file (e.g. main_test.go), either by invoking the built binary via os/exec or by extracting the parsing/formatting logic into a testable helper, covering the golden path and both documented error paths.
beads.acceptance: A new test file exercises: (a) running with no arguments exits with status 2 and prints the "usage: fixture NUMBER [NUMBER...]" message to stderr; (b) running with a non-numeric argument exits with status 2 and prints a "fixture: ... is not a number" message to stderr naming the bad argument; (c) running with valid numeric arguments exits 0 and prints output to stdout containing correctly computed sum, mean, and max values. `make test` / `go test ./...` passes including the new tests. No change to main.go's existing documented CLI behaviour is required by this bead.
